ai.title: Move prompt from State to params in agent runtime
ai.summary: Refactors agent runtime to remove `prompt` from `State` and pass it explicitly via params in `handler-function-type.ts`, `write-file.ts`, `stream-parser.ts`, and `tool-executor.ts`. This decouples prompt data from mutable state, reducing side effects and improving handler isolation. Scope limited to `packages/agent-runtime/src`. No migration needed; internal type alignment only.

eli5.text: The agent runtime stopped stashing the current prompt inside its shared working memory and instead passes that prompt in directly each time a tool runs. As a result, tools like the file writer and the stream parser now receive the prompt as a parameter rather than reading it from the state object, so they no longer rely on that shared, mutable memory to know what they are working on. You would notice nothing as a user today because no behavior changed. This is live today and only shifts how the data flows internally.

ai.title: Move logger out of State
ai.summary: Refactors agent-runtime to remove logger from State. Logger is now passed via ExecuteToolCallParams. Affects run-programmatic-step, stream-parser, tool-executor, and handler-function-type.

eli5.text: The assistant's logging system has been moved out of the main state object and is now passed through the execution parameters instead. This is a behind-the-scenes code cleanup that doesn't change any visible behavior for users today, but makes the code more organized for future development. If you looked at the code, you'd see that the logging functionality is now handled more cleanly throughout the workflow without being tied to the central state management.

ai.title: agentContext moved from State to handler params
ai.summary: agentContext removed from State type in handler-function-type.ts. Handlers receive agentContext as top-level param in tool-executor.ts, add-subgoal.ts, update-subgoal.ts. run-agent-step.ts, run-programmatic-step.ts, stream-parser.ts updated to pass agentContext directly. Internal refactor, no API changes.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal record of what it's working on (its 'agentContext') used to travel tucked inside a larger state object that every step passed around. Now that information is handed directly to the individual tools and step-runners that actually need it, instead of riding along in the shared state. If you looked at the system from the outside, nothing behaves differently today - the assistant still plans and tracks subgoals the same way - but the internal plumbing that moves that tracking data around has been straightened out so each part gets exactly what it asks for, nothing more.

ai.title: Remove messages from programmatic step state
ai.summary: Refactored agent runtime to remove `messages` from `State` in `run-programmatic-step.ts`, `add-message.ts`, `find-files.ts`, and `read-files.ts`. Handlers now directly mutate `agentState.messageHistory`, eliminating redundant state syncing and cloning. This simplifies state management and reduces memory overhead by removing duplicate message arrays.

eli5.text: The agent no longer keeps a duplicate copy of the conversation while it works. Previously, it stored messages in two places: a temporary working list and the main conversation history, then copied them back together. Now it writes directly to the main conversation history, dropping the extra copy. If you watched the process closely you'd see fewer memory hiccups and less redundant bookkeeping behind the scenes.

ai.title: Remove file processing state from agent runtime
ai.summary: Refactored `run-agent-step.ts` and `run-programmatic-step.ts` to eliminate the generic `State` object, passing `fileProcessingState` directly to tool handlers. Updated `handler-function-type.ts` to remove `getLatestState` and `state` params in favor of explicit `fileProcessingState`. Modified `write-file.ts`, `str-replace.ts`, and `create-plan.ts` to consume the direct state reference and return empty state objects. This simplifies state management in the agent runtime by removing indirect state retrieval.

eli5.text: The way the assistant keeps track of file changes while it works has been simplified so there is one clear path for that information instead of a shared stash it had to look up each time. You would not see anything different in the app today, since this just reorganizes how the background steps share file status without changing what they do.

ai.title: Fix CLI input wrapping calculation
ai.summary: Corrected input width calculation in `cli/src/chat.tsx` by removing hardcoded padding subtraction from `Math.max(1, inputWidth - 4)`. Fixes slight wrapping bugs in the CLI chat interface. Code formatting and dependency array structures were also normalized.

eli5.text: When you type a long message in the CLI chat, it was wrapping a little too early, cutting off the last few characters before the text reached the edge of your terminal. The terminal was reserving four extra spaces of blank margin that didn't need to be there, making the usable width slightly smaller than your screen allowed. Now the calculation uses the full width of your terminal, so the text fills the space correctly and lines wrap at the true edge instead of a few columns too soon.

ai.title: Update feedback success message
ai.summary: Feedback success message changed to 'Thanks, your feedback helps! 💖'. Updates showClipboardMessage call in cli/src/components/feedback-container.tsx. Scope limited to CLI feedback container.

eli5.text: When you submit feedback through the CLI, you will now see the message 'Thanks, your feedback helps! 💖' instead of the previous 'Feedback sent ✔' confirmation. This change only affects the pop-up message that appears after you successfully send your feedback - nothing else about how the feedback system works has changed. The update is live today.

ai.title: Disable CLI mode switching UI
ai.summary: Commented out AgentModeToggle rendering in cli/src/components/chat-input-bar.tsx. Hardcoded estimatedToggleWidth to 0 in cli/src/hooks/use-chat-input.ts. Removes interactive mode switching from CLI chat input. Mode switching remains disabled until plan mode bugs resolved.

eli5.text: When you open the assistant in the terminal, the small button that let you flip between modes (like normal chat and a 'plan' mode) no longer appears. The developers pulled the plug on that toggle because the plan mode still has bugs, so right now you stay in whatever mode you started in and can't switch while chatting. If you looked at the chat input at the bottom of the window, the area is just a bit narrower on the left where that toggle used to live.

ai.title: Version 1.0.528 release for the CLI package
ai.summary: Bumps the CLI package version to 1.0.528 in `cli/release/package.json`. This release bundles the 1.0.528 updates, including a new `publish` command for uploading agent templates, validation errors moved to per-message popovers, copy buttons on message blocks, renamed tool params ($toolParams to toolParams, parameters to inputSchema) with WebSocket schema removal, and various agent-runtime refactors that move data like prompt, logger, agentContext, messages, system, and fileProcessingState out of generic State objects into explicit handler parameters. These changes simplify state management in `packages/agent-runtime` and improve CLI UI clarity.
ai.evidence: Commit bd09f6ee modifies only `cli/release/package.json`, changing the `version` field from `1.0.527` to `1.0.528`.

eli5.text: This release makes your coding agent smarter and gives you new ways to save, share, and control it. The editor's 'best-of-n' feature now generates more candidate answers by default (up to 4 normal and 6 maximum) so you get better suggestions, and a new 'publish' command lets you upload your custom agent templates directly to your account. Validation errors now pop up right next to the message that caused them instead of cluttering a banner at the top, clipboard copies happen almost instantly, and a copy button appears on every message block for quick saving of responses. Behind the scenes the agent runtime was cleaned up so prompts, loggers, and context travel through explicit parameters rather than hidden state, which generally makes behavior more predictable. Upgrading gives you faster, clearer, and more reliable interactions with fewer UI glitches and easier agent-template sharing.

ai.title: Refactor tool handlers to async functions
ai.summary: Tool handler signatures in agent-runtime changed from synchronous returns containing a `result` Promise and optional `state` to direct async functions returning an `output` object. This removes the `State` type and simplifies the contract for handlers like `add-message`, `add-subgoal`, and `code-search`. The refactor affects `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/` and associated tests, enforcing a cleaner separation of concerns by eliminating state management from the handler return structure.

eli5.text: If you watched the agent work, nothing now looks or feels different; the behind-the-scenes wiring for how individual agent actions (like adding a note, recording a sub-goal, or searching code) get processed got reorganized. The code that runs each action now returns its result directly instead of wrapping it in a second helper object, which cleans up how the system keeps track of things internally. You would only notice this if you poked at the agent's internal structure: the extra bookkeeping object and its associated type are gone, replaced by a simpler, direct response. This is the kind of change engineers make to keep the system stable and easier to maintain long-term, not something that changes what you see.
